newsitem.title: GERMANY: Turkish children protest visa law across Germany.
newsitem.headline: Turkish children protest visa law across Germany.

text.p: Turkish children across Germany stayed away from school on Thursday to protest against a new law which obliges them to apply for residence permits to remain in the country.
The Association of Turkish Communities in Germany estimated tens of thousands of children had taken part in the protests.

Nearly 500 children, Turkish community leaders and German DGB trade union federation members gathered outside the Berlin City Hall, shouting in German "Children in, Kanther out", referring to Interior Minister Manfred Kanther.
Several children carried banners and wore hand-painted T-shirts with slogans, such as: "Grandpa: In Germany for 40 years, Papa: Berliner, Me: Foreigner?" and "We want equal rights for all children."
In Hamburg, around 100 children formed a human chain around the St Michaelis church in the city centre. Opponents of the new law also held demonstrations in Frankfurt.

Under the rule which came into force last month, children under 16 from Turkey, Tunisia, Morocco and former Yugoslavia now have to apply for visas to visit relatives in Germany and those living here already must obtain a residence permit.
The 2.2 million members of Germany's Turkish community do not have German citizenship, meaning their children now have to apply as "foreigners" for permits.
The government insists the measure was necessary because foreigners were abusing its previously relaxed stance on children visiting relatives in Germany by staying permanently.
Protest organisers said pupils in Recklingshausen, Bielefeld and Essen had also taken part in the schools boycott and one Berlin activist said she would go on hunger strike.
In the southern town of Aschaffenburg, youngsters blocked a main road to demonstrate their opposition to the law.
